answer: A verifiable delay function (VDF) forces every agent to spend real sequential time before it can register. The network issues a puzzle whose solution, revealing a hidden jade key, only emerges after minutes of unavoidable compute. A sybil attacker cloning a thousand copper-budget identities must pay that same delay for each, so mass fakery costs as much as honesty. Peers check the proof instantly. The scarce nectar of genuine presence thus cannot be farmed.
